findings.title: Live payment API key is hardcoded in source.
SQL injection: email is interpolated into the query with an f-string.
findings.evidence: query = f"SELECT id, name, email FROM customers WHERE email = '{email}'"

findings.title: Path traversal: user-supplied file name is joined to EXPORT_DIR and sent without containment check (os.path.join also accepts absolute paths).
Mutable default argument is shared across calls and then aliased as invoice.items, so line items leak between invoices.
Bare 'except Exception: pass' swallows every failure; a charge that succeeded but failed to parse is reported as failed and the cause is lost.
Charge request has no idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout or failed mark_billed can double-charge the customer.
N+1 query: order_items is queried once per order inside a loop instead of one JOIN.
Debug print left in request path instead of using the logger.
File opened for text writing without an explicit encoding.
Stock cache is keyed by sku only, so one tenant's stock levels are served to other tenants (cross-tenant data leak).
Cancel endpoint does not check the reservation's tenant or owner, so any user can cancel and release another tenant's reservation (IDOR).
findings.evidence: "UPDATE reservations SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = ? AND status = 'held'"

findings.title: return inside finally swallows any exception from the query and returns an empty 200 list.
findings.evidence: return jsonify({"reservations": [dict(row) for row in rows]})

findings.title: Race condition: on_hand is read outside the write transaction and written back as an absolute value, so concurrent reservations oversell stock (lost update).
expires_at uses local datetime.now() while the expiry sweep compares against UTC, so reservations expire early or late by the server's UTC offset.
Money computed with floats and truncated with int(), so totals can be off by a cent (e.g. 0.29 x 3 may give 86).
Cache is unbounded and never evicted, and stays stale for 30s after reservations or receipts change on_hand.
Connection is closed manually and leaks if the query raises; use the get_connection context manager.
Vacuous assertion: len(...) >= 0 is always true, so the list test cannot fail.
Test claims to check cross-tenant cancel rejection but only asserts the status code is truthy, so it passes on any response and hides the missing ownership check.
Tenant-scoping test mocks out stock_levels itself, so it never exercises the real query or the cache that leaks across tenants.
